builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
summary: ActiveSecHarness replaces LLM-as-a-judge guardrails and static regex blacklists for tool-using coding agents with deterministic OS/tool guards, HMAC capability tokens, and a 2D taint lattice tracking trust and sensitivity with workspace provenance. The cost is engineering complexity: implementing ring-based permissions, capability tokens, and a provenance ledger is a substantial architectural change to an existing agent harness, not a drop-in filter. It can fail where deterministic policies are incomplete or misconfigured, the N=252 fixture evaluation may not cover novel attack structures, and its perfect ABR/FPR figures are self-reported on a single benchmark without independent replication.
rationale: The architecture directly addresses prompt-injection risk in production coding agents and the deterministic guard layer is feasible without heavy infrastructure, but adopting the full capability-token and taint-lattice system requires workload-specific validation before committing engineering effort.
technique: Neurosymbolic reference monitor for agentic coding harnesses

claims.statement: ActiveSecHarness replaces LLM-as-a-judge guardrails and static regex blacklists for tool-using coding agents with deterministic OS/tool guards, HMAC capability tokens, and a 2D taint lattice tracking trust and sensitivity with workspace provenance. The cost is engineering complexity: implementing ring-based permissions, capability tokens, and a provenance ledger is a substantial architectural change to an existing agent harness, not a drop-in filter. It can fail where deterministic policies are incomplete or misconfigured, the N=252 fixture evaluation may not cover novel attack structures, and its perfect ABR/FPR figures are self-reported on a single benchmark without independent replication.

Deterministic Ring-0 guards decide in 12.7 microseconds versus 142.3 ms for a local LLM judge (approximately 11,200x faster), while blocking all 120 attacks with zero false positives versus the LLM judge refusing 98.3% of benign work.
